title: Exact native YEIS body and black-hole travel

scope.subject: Route body and black-hole destinations through the pinned YEIS reference-frame and camera primitives instead of degrading to host-star travel

research_summary: The existing product can discover YEIS bodies and black holes but main still degrades some targets to their host star or React-only planet model. Reuse the already-adopted pinned MIT YEIS universe/body/camera semantics for exact native travel, with Personal Universe only adapting destination types and product state. Do not add a second camera controller or synthesize cross-scale motion in React.

sources.finding: The verified MIT snapshot is already the selected universe backbone and contains the hierarchical universe, native bodies, black-hole data and camera/autopilot implementation used by the hosted YEIS renderer.
The pinned MIT UI exposes native navigation entry points including system/body and black-hole travel; those semantics can be adapted without copying the whole legacy UI.
React Three Fiber is the existing renderer host and supplies the shared Three scene/frame lifecycle; it should remain host infrastructure rather than become a second cross-scale travel authority.

camera-controls is a mature generic Three.js camera-control component with smooth transitions and interaction handling, but it does not model YEIS reference-frame switching or native celestial-body identity.

search_ladder.conclusion: The already-selected verified MIT YEIS snapshot is the broader full solution and already owns the exact universe hierarchy, native bodies, compact objects and cross-scale camera semantics required by this gap.
React Three Fiber remains the correct host framework for the shared Three.js scene, but it intentionally does not provide astronomical reference-frame or native-body navigation semantics.

Pinned YEIS native travel already defines system/body and black-hole navigation over the same Universe and CameraController state currently hosted by Personal Universe, so those primitives should be reused directly.

camera-controls is a mature generic Three.js alternative for camera motion, but introducing it would duplicate the existing YEIS camera controller while still leaving reference-frame and target identity work unsolved.

candidates.name: Verified MIT YEIS universe backbone
candidates.license: MIT source at pinned commit; retained third-party notices for data/assets
candidates.reason: Keep the already-adopted mother universe as the identity/reference-frame owner. The implementation only needs to expose more of its existing native travel semantics through the product adapter.

candidates.name: Pinned YEIS native body/black-hole travel primitives
candidates.source: Pinned MIT Universe + native camera/UI semantics
candidates.reason: Directly solves exact target identity, star-system frame switching and native camera travel using the same runtime already mounted in the galaxy scene, with no second camera or coordinate system.

candidates.name: camera-controls smooth Three.js camera controller
candidates.reason: Mature motion component but it cannot resolve or switch YEIS astronomical reference frames and would compete with the native CameraController already responsible for galaxy travel.

decision.rationale: Extend the product adapter to expose exact body and black-hole travel that the already-selected pinned MIT YEIS runtime can perform natively. Keep R3F as the host lifecycle and React as product state only; do not add a second camera controller, coordinate system or custom cross-scale flight algorithm.
decision.fallback: If a target is genuinely absent from the pinned runtime, fail visibly or center its known host rather than fabricating a different body identity. Re-evaluate the mother backbone before adding another cross-scale navigation engine.
